newsitem.title: UK: Elf buys over 100,000t gasoline due strike - traders.
newsitem.headline: Elf buys over 100,000t gasoline due strike - traders.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine has scooped up at least 100,000 to 125,000 tonnes of gasoline over the last week to meet production shortfalls from the strike at its three French refineries, traders said on Thursday.

Traders braced for another French buying spree if talks on Thursday fail to end the eight-day-old strike and a threatened nationwide, one-day oil industry strike is carried out on Tuesday, hitting one-eighth of European capacity.
Elf said it did not comment on trading transactions.
"As long as the strike goes on, it's good news (for higher prices)," a trader said.
"(Elf) has bought large quantities," another trader said.
"It's only Elf...At the moment nothing else is being done (by other oil companies)," he said, when asked about buying by other French oil companies before Tuesday.
The rumoured amount is a bit more than the 800,000 barrels, or 95,000 tonnes, of gasoline that traders estimated Elf has lost because of the strike.
One source estimated Elf may have bought close to 150,000 tonnes.

European gasoline prices jumped this week because the French demand is competing with a healthy appetite from the U.S., which has sucked material out of Northwest Europe due to a profitable arbitrage, they said.
A 60,000 tonne gasoline cargo was confirmed sold out of the U.K. on Wednesday destined for the U.S.
European gasoline demand runs at about 3.0 million bpd, according to the International Energy Agency.
"They are definitely buying," said one trader, who said Elf was in the market again on Thursday.

Elf has bought super unleaded, unleaded and leaded material, with the U.K., a traditional exporter, an ideal supplier after inventories swelled ahead of the new U.K. tax on petrol announced November 26, traders said.
Some material was also sold into southern France, traders confirmed.
The three refineries are the 98,000 bpd Grandpuits near Paris, the 128,000 bpd Feyzin near Lyon and the 214,000 bpd Donges in western France.
Unions and management were due to meet on Thursday afternoon over pay and conditions which Elf says it is willing to discuss.
The strike over 330 job cuts at Elf, France's largest oil firm, has crippled a quarter of the country's refining output with few if any signs of it melting.
Industry sources said Elf produces about 100,000 bpd of gasoline and feeds about 60,000 into the French domestic market, which consumes about 350,000 bpd.
Wholesale prices in the Northwest Europe market jumped sharply this week, with barges up $5 on Thursday to $225/$226 on a free-on-board basis.
The impact has been slow to get through to ordinary consumers, in part because of the blockade of depots by French truckers last month, which kept most tanks full.
